correctness.rationale: The Gaussian posterior risk identity is derived explicitly. For all integer p>=0, the exact binomial expression for I_p' has positive coefficients; its second-derivative sign polynomial has one positive constant coefficient and all subsequent coefficients nonpositive with a strictly negative last term. Thus I_p has exactly one inflection, H_p=I_p/I_p'-t first decreases then strictly increases from a negative minimum to infinity, giving one global optimum for all eta>0. Uniform endpoint expansions yield the sharp high-noise placement and regret constants. The standalone verifier checks exact identities for p=0..8 and numerical illustrations; the all-order proof does not depend on those samples.

originality.rationale: The inspected foundational 2014 integrated-Wiener derivative-evaluation paper proves probabilistic Runge–Kutta correspondences, not a global one-noisy-derivative-site optimization law. The inspected 2016 longitudinal-design paper gives the generic trajectory error criterion for direct observations of the target process, not the mixed W(t)/X_p(s) covariance or the all-integer-order placement law. Previous directly observed integrated-Wiener results use a distinct sensor channel and do not imply the present rule. No inspected source contains the claimed exact all-noise uniqueness plus p-dependent boundary exponent; inaccessible historical and unindexed work leave genuine priority uncertainty.

value.rationale: One noisy derivative/base-process evaluation is a motivated resource constraint in integrated-Wiener Gaussian path reconstruction and probabilistic ODE work. The theorem solves the complete all-noise global time-placement problem for the entire integer hierarchy, gives monotonicity and unique optimizers, and identifies the sharp order-dependent high-noise boundary layer and terminal-placement regret; the claims are structural and not a routine finite table or arbitrarily chosen parameter slice.
